neighbours.label: a quantity framed as scarce or limited ('only a few', 'in smaller numbers', 'in limited use', 'a small minority'), as against the same phrase framed as abundant
fire: The orchid is rare in the wild, and only a few dozen plants survive on the island.
Because of the cost, the car was made in smaller numbers than its rivals.
Today the old printing presses are in limited use, mostly in art studios.
The disease is very uncommon, striking only a handful of children each year.
In the survey, just a tiny fraction of the farmers grew organic crops.
The species is now scarce, with only a few pairs nesting along the coast.
Tickets were issued in very small quantities, so most fans missed out.
For years the medicine was produced in low volumes and was hard to find.
quiet: The orchid is common in the wild, and thousands of plants grow on the island.
Because of the low price, the car was made in larger numbers than its rivals.
Today the old printing presses are in wide use, even in big factories.
The disease is very widespread, striking millions of children each year.
In the survey, the great majority of the farmers grew organic crops.
The species is now abundant, with many pairs nesting along the coast.
Tickets were issued in huge quantities, so every fan got a seat.
For years the medicine was produced in high volumes and was easy to find.

predictions: fire 0.15-0.5 on the scarcity word or the noun after it ('few', 'numbers', 'use'); the same sentences with 'many', 'larger', 'wide', 'large majority' below 0.1
notes: Card: 'but least common', 'in limited use', 'in smaller numbers', 'a small minority', 'rare genetic disorder, affecting'; the - pole promotes ' rare', ' narrow', ' fewer'. Probe: 'built in smaller numbers' 0.482, 'only a few hundred people' 0.404, 'limited use' 0.181, 'small minority' 0.170; abundant versions 0.005-0.093.
